transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I hope it's okay that I'm here. I might just be overthinking things, but... I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I'm a camera operator and video editor, and, well, it's actually a little embarrassing to admit. I guess what finally scared me into coming in is that I just keep making these... really silly technical mistakes. Things I absolutely know better than to make. 

Like, I'll label a camera card wrong, or I'll miss a timecode note. Just little things, mostly! But recently I exported a client cut with the wrong lower-third, and the worst part is I swear I had just checked it before sending it off. I always want to do a good job and keep my clients happy, so slipping up like that really worried me. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm in the right place for this.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed lately?

Oh, um, no, I wouldn't say anxious. I mean, I don't think so? I definitely don't want to sound like I'm complaining! I know everyone gets a little stressed at work sometimes, right? 

But no, I don't feel overwhelmed, really. Just... maybe a little frustrated with myself for not catching those little mistakes when I know I can do better. I always try to keep a really positive attitude on set and in the edit bay, so I don't think it's an anxiety thing. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory outside of work?

Um, outside of work? No, I don't think so. I mean, my memory is usually pretty good, I think! I manage to keep track of my personal life and errands just fine. 

It's really just those silly little slip-ups when I'm editing or on set. I hope that's okay to say? Like, I definitely don't want to make it sound like my whole life is falling apart or anything, because at home I feel like I'm doing a pretty good job keeping everything together. I haven't noticed any big memory issues there. Is it normal for it to just happen at work? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Oh, no, definitely not sad! I'm actually a pretty upbeat person, I think. I mean, I really try to be. I love my job, and I have great friends, so I don't really have any reason to feel down, you know? 

I hope I'm not giving the wrong impression—I'm really not depressed or anything like that. I'm usually the one trying to keep the energy up in the edit room! It's just those frustrating little mistakes that have been bugging me. But overall, my mood is totally fine. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering these right for you.
Do you have trouble focusing or concentrating on tasks?

Um, focusing? No, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that. Actually, I think I'm usually pretty good at locking in, especially when I'm cutting a scene together. I can sit at the monitors and just zero in on the footage for a really long time. 

I mean, I hope that doesn't sound like I'm bragging! I just mean I don't really struggle to pay attention to the task itself. My concentration is usually right there when I need it to be. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of example you were looking for.
Have you noticed any difficulty learning new things recently?

Um, learning new things? No, I don't think so. I actually really like learning new techniques for editing, or, you know, getting the hang of a new software update when we have to. I feel like I pick things up pretty quickly!

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm trying to, like, paint myself as perfect or anything. I just haven't really noticed any roadblocks when it comes to learning. I'm usually pretty eager to figure out a new workflow if it helps the team. Is that okay? Like, is it normal that I don't have an issue with that part? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of how things are going.
Do you ever feel mentally foggy or like your thinking is cloudy?

Um, foggy? No, I don't think so. Honestly, my brain usually feels pretty clear. If anything, it's usually going a little fast, you know? But definitely not cloudy. I feel like I stay pretty sharp, especially when I'm working on a tight deadline or juggling a bunch of different clips. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that issue? Like, I really don't want to mess up your evaluation by not having these things you're asking about. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right information. Is that a good answer?
Have you been feeling unusually tired lately?

Um, tired? No, honestly, I haven't. If anything, I'm kind of the opposite? I usually have a ton of energy, even when we have really long days on set or I'm pulling a late shift in the editing bay. I don't really get that exhausted feeling during the day. 

I really hope it's not frustrating that I keep saying no to all these things! I promise I'm really thinking about your questions. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need. Is it okay that my energy levels are pretty high? I just hope I'm not messing up the assessment by not having these specific issues... is this still helpful for you?
Do you think you're being as detail-oriented as you usually are when you're working on editing tasks?

Um, detail-oriented... well, I try to be. I really do. But... um, actually, this is kind of what finally scared me into coming in to see you. I really hate admitting this, because I pride myself on my work, but I keep making these really dumb technical mistakes. 

Like, things I absolutely know better than to make. I've been labeling camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note from the director. And just last week, I exported a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, even after I thought I had checked it. It's so embarrassing. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just bad at my job. I promise I'm usually really good at what I do! It's just... lately, these little things are slipping through, and it's making me so anxious that I'm letting the team down. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this part? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even the parts I'm not proud of.
Are the technical mistakes you're making at work things that you knew how to do correctly in the past?

Oh, yes, absolutely. Um, that's what makes it so frustrating, honestly. I've been doing this for years, and these are basically day-one skills. Like, I could usually do all of that in my sleep. So I definitely know how to do them right... I just, for some reason, am rushing past them or missing them right now. 

I really hope it doesn't make me sound incompetent? I promise I'm normally very reliable with all the technical stuff, and my supervisors usually love my work. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the way you need me to... did that make sense? Is that what you were asking?
Do you think you're fully paying attention when you're making these technical mistakes?

Um, paying attention... well, I really try to. I always want to give my full focus to my work. But, um... I guess maybe I'm not? Or my brain just kind of skips over things? 

Like I was saying before, that's what really scared me into making this appointment. I keep making these dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. It's like I'll look right at a camera card and just label it wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note from the director even if I'm looking at the screen. Or that client cut I exported with the wrong lower-third... I really thought I had checked it, but clearly my attention must have slipped somewhere. 

I hope I'm explaining this right. I don't want it to sound like I don't care about my job, because I really, really do. I just... I guess my focus isn't where it needs to be when I'm doing those steps. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think you're remembering the procedures and protocols correctly when you're making these technical mistakes, but just not executing them right?

Um, yes, exactly. I remember the procedures perfectly. That's actually what's so embarrassing about it. 

Like I was just mentioning with the camera cards and the timecode notes... I know exactly what the protocols are. I know exactly how to do them. It's just the execution that's somehow going wrong. Even with that client cut I was telling you about, with the wrong lower-third graphic... I knew the right procedure, and I even checked it! But I still somehow executed it wrong. 

That disconnect between knowing what to do and actually doing it right is really what finally scared me into coming in to see you. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just... I really want to make sure you know that I *do* know my job, and I'm not just being careless on purpose. I really try hard to do things right. Does that make sense? Am I explaining that the way you need me to?
Do you think you're forgetting what you're supposed to do at the moment you're making these technical mistakes?

Um, no, I don't think I'm forgetting in the moment. I really don't. Like I said, I know exactly what I'm supposed to be doing. It's not like my mind just goes blank or I suddenly don't know the steps. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm giving you all these confusing answers. I just... I want to be really clear that I do know my job and I'm not, like, losing my memory or anything. It's just that the mistakes happen anyway, even when I know what to do. I hope that's okay? Is that helpful for you to know?
Are the tasks where you're making mistakes things that you normally do automatically, without having to think about each step?

Um, well... I guess some of them are pretty automatic? Like, I've been editing for a while, so a lot of the basic steps are just muscle memory at this point. 

But I don't want you to think I'm just zoning out and letting autopilot take over, because I really do try to stay present and focused on every little detail. I mean, maybe I get a little too comfortable with the routine stuff sometimes? I'm not sure. I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm just coasting through my work. I really take it seriously. Does that sound like what you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you think your mistakes are happening because you're not paying enough attention to the details or because you're having trouble processing the information correctly?

Um, well... I really hope it's not that I'm not paying enough attention. I mean, I try *so* hard to focus on the details. I really do. But... I guess it might be that? 

Like I was saying before, that's what finally scared me into coming in. I just... I keep making these dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. Like, you know, labeling the camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note, or... or exporting that client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, even after I've literally just checked it. 

I guess when you put it like that, it does sound like I'm missing details, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm just a careless person who doesn't care about her work. I care so much. But the details just... slip by me somehow, even when I'm looking right at them. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of processing issue you mean, or is that just me not paying enough attention? I'm sorry, I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Do you think you're seeing all the details in front of you when you're working, but just not using them correctly?

Um, I'm not totally sure? I mean, I *feel* like I'm seeing everything. I look at the screen, I see the clips, I see the notes... I don't feel like my vision is blurring or I'm literally blind to things on the monitor. 

But I guess... maybe I'm not using the information right? Or maybe I'm seeing it but it's just not clicking in my brain the way it should? I really don't want it to sound like I'm incompetent or that I don't know how to use my editing software, because I promise I do. It's just... sometimes the dots don't connect in the moment, even if all the pieces are right there in front of me. 

Does that sound like what you're asking? I'm sorry, I feel like I'm doing a terrible job of explaining this. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can figure out what's wrong with me. Am I making any sense at all?
Do you think you're forgetting things you've learned in the past, or just not applying them correctly in the moment?

Um... I don't think I'm forgetting things. I really hope I'm not, anyway. I've been doing this for a long time, and I know the software and the workflows inside and out. I promise I know what I'm doing. 

I guess... maybe it's just not applying it right in the moment? Like, the knowledge is there in my head, but when I'm actually cutting a sequence and moving fast, sometimes my brain just... skips a step? I don't want you to think I'm losing my memory or that my skills are fading, because I really do try to stay on top of everything. It's just... in the heat of the moment, it doesn't always translate perfectly. 

Is that okay? I mean, does that make sense for what you're trying to figure out? I just want to make sure I'm not leading you down the wrong path or making myself sound like I don't know my job. I really do know my job.
Do you think your brain is fully engaged when you're performing these routine editing tasks?

Um, well... I'd like to think it is? I mean, I really try to stay fully engaged. I care about my projects so much, so I'm always trying to give them my absolute full attention. 

But... I guess I'm not entirely sure how to tell if it's *fully* engaged? Like, if it's a really routine task, something I've done a million times like syncing audio or organizing bins, maybe my mind wanders a tiny bit? But not in a bad way! I promise I'm not just zoning out or ignoring my responsibilities. I'm always trying to do my best, it's just... I don't know, maybe it's normal to not be at one hundred percent intensity for the really repetitive stuff? 

I hope I'm not making it sound like I don't care about my work, because I really, really do. I just don't know for sure if my brain is completely locked in every single second. Is that... does that make sense? Is that what you were asking me?
Do you think you would make the same mistakes if you were to deliberately slow down and double-check your work?

Um, well... I mean, if I deliberately slowed down and double-checked everything... I guess I probably wouldn't make those mistakes? I mean, I try to double-check things anyway, I really do. I don't want you to think I just rush through and throw things together without caring. 

But, you know, in this industry, the deadlines are so tight, and they always need everything yesterday, so slowing down isn't always... an option? But if I *could* take my time, I'm sure I'd catch those little things. I'm actually very detail-oriented when I have the time to be! 

Does that... does that answer your question? I just really don't want to sound like I'm careless with my work. I hope I'm explaining this okay?
Do you think you would still make these mistakes if you had more time to think through each step?

Um... I guess if I had unlimited time, maybe not? I mean, I try so hard to think through every step, I really do. But... well, I guess I should just be honest. What actually finally scared me into making this appointment is that... even when I think I'm checking things, I'm still making these really dumb technical mistakes. 

Mistakes I absolutely know better than to make! Like, I'll label the camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note from the director. Or, um, the other day I exported a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, and the worst part is I *did* check it before I sent it. I swear I looked right at it. 

I just... I don't want you to think I'm bad at my job, because I've been doing this a long time and I'm usually so careful. But it's just really embarrassing to keep doing things like that. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm not making myself sound completely incompetent...
